generator_semantics: Independent JS translation of configuration-pair-reject-v1: XorShift64* 64-bit stream, rejection-sampled bounded integers, Fisher-Yates stub shuffle, reject self-loops/duplicate edges, canonical sort, degree invariant check.
source_manifest: docs/research/quantum/benchmarks/QCOMP-RRG-COHORT-001.json at branch research/qcomp-rrg-cohort-001 before this receipt
limitations: This runs an independent JavaScript translation, not the Rust generator binary; it verifies the specified algorithm semantics but not Rust compilation or byte-for-byte parity.
Twenty seeds per size is a generator smoke sample, not a statistical validation of the configuration-model distribution and not the complete 200-per-size paper-shaped cohort.
FNV-1a edge-list fingerprints are non-cryptographic screening IDs, not provenance hashes. A Rust run must record SHA-256 of each materialized DIMACS byte stream.
No solver, QAOA expectation calculation, QPU, or performance comparison was run.

distributional_sanity_check.status: independent-javascript-translation-only; not Rust execution or certification
distributional_sanity_check.seed_derivation: SplitMix64-derived seed words starting from index 123456789; each seed initializes the same XorShift64* stream used by the proposed Rust generator

graph_isomorphism_classes.exact_reference: There are 70 labeled simple 3-regular graphs on six vertices: 10 labeled K3,3 graphs and 60 labeled triangular-prism graphs. Each simple graph has (3!)^6 stub pairings, so uniform configuration-model pairing conditioned on simplicity gives the 1/7 versus 6/7 probabilities.

observed_pairing_attempts.note: The 18 stubs have 17!! = 34,459,425 pairings; 70 simple labelled 3-regular graphs each correspond to (3!)^6 = 46,656 stub pairings.

diagnostics.interpretation: No gross small-N frequency discrepancy appeared in this sample; a passing diagnostic is not proof of uniform sampling at all sizes.

limitations: This 100,000-sample audit executed an independent JavaScript translation, not the Rust generator.
A deterministic PRNG stream and seed set are not independent true random draws; the exercise is a regression/sanity check rather than statistical certification.
Small-N results do not establish distributional correctness for all N, degrees, or rejection budgets.
The new Rust unit test uses 5,000 sequential seeds and a deliberately coarse frequency tolerance; its execution remains unconfirmed until a Rust toolchain is available.

brute_force_enumeration_validation.method: Enumerate all 2^15 edge-presence bitmasks on six labeled vertices, retain exactly those with every vertex degree 3, then classify by triangle presence.
brute_force_enumeration_validation.result: Exact combinatorial class counts used for the 1/7 versus 6/7 reference were independently reproduced by exhaustive enumeration in this session.

canonical_rust_implementation.seed_stream_alignment: The canonical Rust API was updated to use the same XorShift64* stream, rejection-sampled Fisher-Yates bounded draw and in-place re-shuffle semantics as this independent JS translation. Exact Rust-to-JS graph-byte parity remains unverified until Rust is executable. A static test review also fixed a stub-ceiling fixture that previously would have triggered the vertex ceiling first; the fixture now uses n=100000,d=12 to isolate the stub-limit error.
canonical_rust_implementation.failure_provenance: Generator exhaustion error now preserves vertex_count, degree, seed and max_attempts; CLI emits a structured failure receipt to stderr and keeps graph stdout empty on failure. Rust execution remains unverified.

preflight_origin.consolidation_note: The initial Rust candidate used a fresh stub clone per retry and a different rejection-bounded draw implementation, so these records were never treated as Rust output-parity evidence. The canonical Rust implementation has since been aligned to the JS preflight semantics, but no byte-by-byte Rust regeneration has been executed.
